module_intro: Treats the dealing range as 'the container that filters everything': range selection discipline, equilibrium/premium/discount, range expansion/contraction, liquidity relative to premium/discount, PD arrays relative to premium/discount, and the two symmetric execution frameworks (Bullish Discount Framework, Bearish Premium Framework).
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Requires Beginner Module 7 (Fibonacci & OTE, premium/discount) and Intermediate Modules 1-5.
module_objectives: Select the correct dealing range for the timeframe and narrative being traded.
Locate equilibrium and correctly label premium and discount halves.
Recognise range expansion and range contraction and their implications for array relevance.
Filter liquidity objectives and PD arrays according to their location in premium or discount.
Apply the bullish-discount and bearish-premium frameworks consistently.
Avoid the common error of taking long setups in deep premium or short setups in deep discount without strong overriding context.
Update the dealing range when external structure expands and holds.

concepts.name: The Dealing Range - Selection Discipline
concepts.definition: A dealing range is the price territory bounded by a significant swing high (range high) and a significant swing low (range low). Equilibrium is the exact 50 % midpoint of that range.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: A dealing range is the price territory bounded by a significant swing high (range high) and a significant swing low (range low). Equilibrium is the exact 50 % midpoint of that range.

raw_sections.Definition (Unchanged): A dealing range is the price territory bounded by a significant swing high (range high) and a significant swing low (range low). Equilibrium is the exact 50 % midpoint of that range.
raw_sections.Selecting the Correct Range:
The most common intermediate error is marking an arbitrary or too-narrow range. Selection guidelines:

- Prefer the range whose boundaries have been tested or have engineered liquidity (sweeps of both sides raise confidence that the range is "active").

- Align the range with the timeframe of the narrative being traded. A 15-minute execution model should reference a 15-minute or 1-hour dealing range that itself sits inside a higher-timeframe container.

- When nested ranges exist, keep the higher-timeframe range in view. A long that is in discount on the 1-hour but deep in premium on the daily requires additional justification.

- Update the range when price expands beyond a boundary with displacement and the new extreme holds. The old boundary is retired; a new container is defined.
raw_sections.Nested / Fractal Ranges: Dealing ranges nest. The daily range lives inside the weekly range; the 1-hour range lives inside the daily. Intermediate analysis maintains awareness of at least two levels so that a local discount is not mistaken for a higher-timeframe discount.

concepts.name: Equilibrium, Premium and Discount
concepts.definition:
Equilibrium = (Range High + Range Low) / 2.

Premium = the upper half of the range (price above equilibrium). Relative to the container, price is expensive.

Discount = the lower half of the range (price below equilibrium). Relative to the container, price is cheap.

raw_sections.Core Intermediate Rule: Seek long (bullish) setups preferentially when price is in discount. Seek short (bearish) setups preferentially when price is in premium. This single filter eliminates a large class of low-quality locations.
raw_sections.Extremes: The deepest portions of premium and discount (roughly the outer 20 - 25 % of the range, often overlapping the 79 % / 21 % Fibonacci region of the range) are the highest-conviction areas for mean-reversion-style entries in the direction of the higher-timeframe bias, provided displacement and structure confirm.

raw_sections.Expansion: Range expansion occurs when price moves forcefully away from equilibrium or from a prior consolidation, creating new extremes, displacement and often Fair Value Gaps. Expansion is the phase in which external liquidity is frequently targeted and in which new Order Blocks and FVGs are born.
raw_sections.Contraction: Range contraction occurs when price compresses, volatility declines and the market builds or rebalances inside a tighter container. Contraction often precedes the next expansion. Trading deep inside prolonged contraction without evidence of displacement is a common intermediate error.
raw_sections.Implications for Arrays: During expansion, newly formed PD arrays (OBs, FVGs) in the direction of the expansion are higher priority. During contraction, older arrays inside the range may be revisited, but the probability of a sustained directional move is lower until expansion resumes.

concepts.name: Liquidity Relative to Premium and Discount

raw_sections.Filtering Liquidity Objectives: Buy-side liquidity that sits in premium is a natural target for a bearish narrative. Sell-side liquidity that sits in discount is a natural target for a bullish narrative. Liquidity that sits against the higher-timeframe bias and in the "wrong" half of the range is lower priority.
raw_sections.Sequential Reading: A common high-quality sequence is: price in discount -> raid of sell-side liquidity -> displacement higher -> expansion toward buy-side liquidity that may itself sit in premium or at the range high (external). The premium/discount filter helps the trader accept that the final target can be in premium even though the entry was taken in discount.

concepts.name: PD Arrays Relative to Premium and Discount

raw_sections.The Filter Applied to Every Array:
Every Order Block, Fair Value Gap, Breaker and Mitigation concept is graded by its location:

678. Bullish PD arrays (bullish OB, bullish FVG, bullish Breaker) are highest quality in discount.

679. Bearish PD arrays (bearish OB, bearish FVG, bearish Breaker) are highest quality in premium.
raw_sections.Wrong-Half Arrays: A bullish Order Block sitting in deep premium is fighting the dealing-range location filter. It may still work if higher-timeframe context is overwhelmingly bullish, but it is lower probability and requires stronger confluence. Intermediate discipline is to prefer the array that is both high-quality in formation and correctly located.

strategies.name: Bullish Discount Framework

context.htf_bias_required: Higher-timeframe bias is bullish (or at least not bearish).
context.other_context: Price is trading in the discount half of the active dealing range (or has just raided sell-side liquidity and is returning into discount).

setup: Identify the dealing range and confirm price is in (or returning to) discount.
Note sell-side liquidity that has been or is being raided.
Wait for bullish displacement and an internal or external Market Structure Shift.
Locate the PD array created by that displacement (FVG and/or Order Block) that sits in discount.
strategies.entry_condition: Enter on the retracement into that array (refined by Consequent Encroachment or lower-timeframe confirmation).
strategies.invalidation_or_stop: A decisive close back below the origin of the bullish displacement or below the dealing-range low (if that low was the structural reference) challenges the bullish discount idea.
strategies.target_or_exit: Target first internal buy-side liquidity, then external buy-side liquidity consistent with the Draw on Liquidity.

strategies.name: Bearish Premium Framework

context.htf_bias_required: Higher-timeframe bias is bearish (or at least not bullish).
context.other_context: Price is trading in the premium half of the active dealing range (or has just raided buy-side liquidity and is returning into premium).

setup: Identify the dealing range and confirm price is in (or returning to) premium.
Note buy-side liquidity that has been or is being raided.
Wait for bearish displacement and a Market Structure Shift.
Locate the PD array created by that displacement that sits in premium.
strategies.entry_condition: Enter on the retracement into that array.
strategies.invalidation_or_stop: A decisive close back above the origin of the bearish displacement or above the dealing-range high challenges the bearish premium idea.
strategies.target_or_exit: Target first internal sell-side liquidity, then external sell-side liquidity.

examples.content:
Context: Daily bias bullish. Active 1-hour dealing range: 1.0800 - 1.1000. Equilibrium = 1.0900.

Price is currently at 1.0860 (discount). A bullish FVG and Order Block overlap between 1.0845 - 1.0865 after a sell-side liquidity raid and displacement.

Assessment: The arrays sit in discount, the bias is bullish, liquidity has been taken, and displacement + MSS are present. This is a high-quality location under the bullish discount framework.

Counter-example: The same arrays form, but price is at 1.0960 (premium) after a shallow pullback. Even with a bullish daily bias, the location is in premium. The intermediate student treats the setup as lower quality and either waits for a deeper retracement into discount or requires exceptional additional confluence before engagement.
examples.interpretation_given_in_text: Applies the premium/discount filter to a concrete scenario to select the higher-quality setup.

relationships.statement: The dealing range is the master container. Equilibrium divides it into premium and discount. That division filters every liquidity pool (Module 2) and every PD array (Modules 4 - 5). Expansion and contraction describe the volatility regime inside the container and influence which arrays are newly formed versus merely being revisited. The bullish-discount and bearish-premium frameworks convert the filter into a repeatable decision process. Multi-timeframe nested ranges (Module 1) keep the local filter subordinate to the higher-timeframe narrative.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Trading deep inside prolonged contraction without evidence of displacement beginning frequently results in being caught in chop; avoid entries during deep contraction without emerging displacement evidence.

key_terms: Dealing range - price container defined by significant swing high and swing low.
Equilibrium - exact 50 % midpoint of the dealing range.
Premium - upper half of the range (price expensive relative to the container).
Discount - lower half of the range (price cheap relative to the container).
Range expansion - forceful movement that creates new extremes and new PD arrays.
Range contraction - compression of range and volatility, often preceding expansion.
Bullish discount framework - long setups preferentially taken in discount after liquidity + displacement + MSS.
Bearish premium framework - short setups preferentially taken in premium after liquidity + displacement + MSS.
module_review_notes.beginner_summary: Beginner teaching introduced premium and discount as the halves of a range. Intermediate teaching makes the dealing-range selection disciplined, nests ranges across timeframes, links expansion/contraction to array formation, and converts the filter into explicit bullish-discount and bearish-premium decision frameworks that govern every PD array and liquidity objective.
module_review_notes.concept_relationships_summary: Structure (Module 1) defines the boundaries of the range. Liquidity (Module 2) is filtered by which half of the range it occupies. Displacement and MSS (Module 3) create the PD arrays that are then graded by premium/discount location (Modules 4 - 5). The frameworks in this module are the practical synthesis that decides which of those arrays are allowed to generate trades.
module_review_notes.practical_chart_exercise:
Before the next session:

- On the daily and 1-hour charts mark the active dealing ranges and their equilibrium levels.

- Note whether price is currently in premium or discount on each timeframe.

- List the nearest unmitigated PD arrays and classify each as correctly or incorrectly located for a long and for a short.

- Identify any expansion or contraction phase currently in progress.

- Write the preferred bullish-discount or bearish-premium sequence that would be required before engagement.

- After the session, record whether price respected the premium/discount filter and what that implies for the next session's range definition.
self_test_questions: How is equilibrium calculated and why does it matter?
What is the core intermediate rule relating trade direction to premium and discount?
How should a trader treat a high-quality bullish Order Block that sits in deep premium?
What typically characterises range expansion versus range contraction?
Outline the preferred sequence of the bullish discount framework.
When should the dealing range itself be updated?
common_misconceptions: "Any range high and low will do." - False. Selection must reflect meaningful, preferably liquidity-tested boundaries.
"If the daily is bullish I can buy anywhere." - False. Location inside the operating dealing range still matters.
"Premium and discount are absolute." - False. They are relative to the chosen container; nested ranges can disagree.
"Once in discount the long is automatic." - False. Liquidity, displacement and MSS are still required.
"The dealing range never changes." - False. Expansion that holds creates a new container.
